note: Set A captures the key mechanical facts — the louvers close through a rotational movement driven by a Nitinol wire actuator and that movement requires no additional energy sources — which Set B omits entirely. Set B instead offers a 'phototrophic movement' claim whose quote only discusses a design paradigm and does not support the attribute, and it never states the actual actuation mechanism. Both sets repeat the 20% glazing fact, and in both the second instance mis-binds the percentage as an 'area'. Set A's remaining weakness is that two quotes paraphrase 'south façade' as 'southern façade'.
remarks: Both sets state the 20% figure twice (once correctly as a proportion of the southern façade, once wrongly as 'operable glazing area'); the figure is a proportion of façade area, not an area value. Both bind 'material | Nitinol wire' to a quote that describes Dynalloy Inc.'s product line rather than the screen itself — defensible but weakly quoted. Set A's quotes for the energy-source and actuation-method claims are not verbatim ('southern façade' where the page reads 'south façade'). Neither set captures the screen's stated functions (insulate from direct solar radiation, control reflected light, allow cross ventilation, maintain privacy) or the DIVA-for-Rhino analysis basis.
